zadanie: A 10-by-12-inch page has margins of 1.5 inches on all sides. What fraction of the area of the page is taken up by the margins? Express your answer as a common fraction.
oczekiwana_odpowiedz: A 10-by-12-inch paper will have an area of $10 \cdot 12 = 120$ square inches. If that paper has 1.5 inch margins on all sides, then the portion of the paper that is not covered by margins will be a rectangular section with length $12 - 2(1.5) = 9$ inches and width $10 - 2(1.5) = 7$ inches. Thus, $9 \cdot 7 = 63$ square inches of the paper will not be taken up by the margins. Since the paper has a total area of $120$ square in, this means that $120-63=57$ square inches of the page is taken up by margins. Thus, margins take up $\dfrac{57}{120}=\boxed{\dfrac{19}{40}}$ of the page.

A 10-by-12-inch page has margins of 1.5 inches on all sides. What fraction of the area of the page is taken up by the margins? Express your answer as a common fraction.
[AI]:
To find the fraction of the area of the page taken up by the margins, I will first calculate the total area of the page and then calculate the area of the inner (non-margin) part of the page.

1.  **Calculate the total area of the page:**
    The page dimensions are 10 inches by 12 inches.
    Total Area = $10 \times 12 = 120$ square inches.

2.  **Calculate the dimensions and area of the inner part:**
    The margins are 1.5 inches on all sides. This means we subtract 1.5 inches twice (once for each side) from both the width and the height.
    Inner Width = $10 - (1.5 + 1.5) = 10 - 3 = 7$ inches.
    Inner Height = $12 - (1.5 + 1.5) = 12 - 3 = 9$ inches.
    Inner Area = $7 \times 9 = 63$ square inches.

3.  **Calculate the area of the margins:**
    Margin Area = Total Area - Inner Area
    Margin Area = $120 - 63 = 57$ square inches.

4.  **Calculate the fraction of the total area taken up by the margins:**
    Fraction = $\frac{\text{Margin Area}}{\text{Total Area}} = \frac{57}{120}$.

5.  **Simplify the fraction:**
    Both 57 and 120 are divisible by 3.
    $57 \div 3 = 19$
    $120 \div 3 = 40$
    The simplified fraction is $\frac{19}{40}$.

Final check:
Total area: $10 \times 12 = 120$.
Inner area: $(10 - 3) \times (12 - 3) = 7 \times 9 = 63$.
Margin area: $120 - 63 = 57$.
Fraction: $57/120 = 19/40$.

The fraction of the area of the page taken up by the margins is $\frac{19}{40}$.
